title: Pointwise fibre criterion for flatness with finitely presented source
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $p:X\to S$, $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ such that $q\circ f=p$. Assume that $p$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and that $q$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix $x\in X$, put $y=f(x)$ and $s=p(x)$, and let $f_s:X_s\to Y_s$ be the induced map of scheme-theoretic fibres over $s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product]. Regard $x$ as the corresponding point of $X_s$. If $p$ is flat at $x$ and $f_s$ is flat at $x$, then $f$ is flat at $x$ and $q$ is flat at $y$ [def-weil-flat-morphism].

proof.text: Write R = O_{S,p(x)}, B = O_{Y,f(x)}, C = O_{X,x}. Stalk-map composition identifies the composite R → B → C with the given R-flat stalk map [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition]. Choose affine opens V around p(x) and U around x mapping into V. Their section map A → D is finitely presented. The germ maps identify R and C as A_a and D_c [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. Localize A → D at A minus a; finite presentation is preserved [lem-trf-localization-finite-presentation-ring-map]. This set maps outside c, so localization transitivity [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] exhibits C as a localization of that finitely presented R-algebra. Germ compatibility proves the scalar tower. Mathlib supplies essential finite type of R → B directly [lem-trf-locally-finite-type-stalk-essentially-finite-type].

The fibre projections have surjective stalk maps with kernels m_R B and m_R C [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient]. The fibre map and projections form a commuting square by the pullback projection equation; the general commuting-stalk-square lemma for locally ringed spaces, proved from stalk-map composition and point congruences and specialized to the underlying locally ringed spaces, gives the commuting square of ring maps [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition]. The first isomorphism theorem identifies the quotient map B/m_R B → C/m_R C with the given fibre stalk map, conjugated by the two quotient equivalences. Composition with bijective ring maps preserves flatness, so the quotient map is flat.

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-local-closed-fibre-approximation] to R → B. Obtain a local, essentially finitely presented R-algebra T and a surjective local R-algebra map u:T → B, inducing the specified equivalence T/m_R T ≅ B/m_R B. Give C its T-action through B. Transport the flat quotient map in step 2 across this equivalence, checking the formula on each class [t]. The standard quotient-tensor equivalence identifies C/m_R C with (T/m_R T) tensor_T C, with this precise action. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre] to R → T → C and M=C, using the two localization models, R-flatness of C, and its nonzero rank-one free C-module structure. This gives T R-flat and C T-flat.

The local flat map T → C is faithfully flat [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective], so its algebra map is injective: the faithful scalar action is the instance obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective]. Since T → C factors through u, u is injective and hence bijective. Compose R → T with the bijective u to obtain flatness of R → B. Cancel u from the flat composite T → B → C, using the inverse ring equivalence, to obtain flatness of B → C. These are exactly the two requested pointwise flatness conclusions.
